_how_to_add: Every thread that ships a feature appends one entry to the END of `entries`, in the same PR. Fields: id (unique, kebab-case), date (YYYY-MM-DD), title, pr (number or null), assignments (ids from assignments.json that this feature practises, may be []), where (repo paths), how (2-4 short plain-English bullets), demo (title + lines; each line has kind cmd|out|note and text). Never put emails, keys or connection strings in it. Optional: status_updates, a list of {assignment, status (todo|doing|done), note, at (ISO time with timezone, e.g. 2026-11-12T16:40:00Z)} to move the admin's assignments on the God mode board. Only claim what is true: site work that practises an assignment is 'doing', never 'done'; 'done' is only for when the admin's own deliverable is submitted. Whichever is newest wins, this update or the admin's own click.

entries.title: The site itself: React page, Python API, Postgres
how: Same three parts as P1: a React page (Vite) calls a FastAPI backend, which saves rows in Postgres.
Every route lives on one router under /api/fde, so it can later be mounted inside sunny-side.
Tables start with fde_ so they can share a database with other apps.

demo.title: Call the API yourself, like P1's curl POST

lines.text: curl https://fde-learnings.onrender.com/api/fde/weeks
[{"id":"week-01","number":1,"title":"Programming fundamentals",...}]
GET reads rows; the site's React page makes this same call and draws the result.

entries.title: Deployed: API on Render, site on Vercel, database on Neon
how: Render builds the API from the Dockerfile on every push to main; Vercel builds the frontend folder.
All settings come from environment variables set in each host's dashboard, never from code.
The backend tidies a pasted Neon string (quotes, psql prefix, line breaks) and ignores trailing slashes in CORS_ORIGINS.

demo.title: Check the live API is up

lines.text: curl https://fde-learnings.onrender.com/health
{"ok":true}
On Render's free plan the first call after a quiet spell takes about a minute while it wakes.

entries.title: Voice quiz on LiveKit
how: The API hands the browser a 15-minute LiveKit token for a private room, and asks LiveKit to send the fde-voice-quiz agent in.
The agent is a P2-style voice bot: speech-to-text, then the LLM, then text-to-speech, reading the week's questions.
Keys live only in the API's and worker's environment.

demo.title: What happens when you press Start call

lines.text: POST /api/fde/weeks/week-02/voice-quiz/token
{"url":"wss://<project>.livekit.cloud","token":"eyJ…","room":"fde-quiz-week-02-u7"}
The browser joins that room; the agent joins too and starts asking.

entries.title: Shared-secret callback from the voice worker
how: When a quiz call ends, the worker POSTs the score to the API, like P3's post-call webhook.
It sends a shared secret in the X-Worker-Key header; the API compares it in constant time and rejects anything else, as P5's Lambda must.

demo.title: A request with the wrong key is rejected

lines.text: curl -X POST $API/api/fde/internal/weeks/week-02/voice-quiz/result -H 'X-Worker-Key: wrong' -d '{…}'
401 {"detail":"Bad worker key."}
With the right key the score is saved and shows on the learner's page.

entries.title: Coursera-style course: modules, readings, quizzes, 18 diagrams
how: Each week is a JSON file split into modules of lessons, readings, practice quizzes, a graded quiz (80% to pass) and the project.
Quizzes are marked on the server, so answers never reach the browser.
Diagrams are hand-drawn SVG components, so they stay sharp and follow the theme.

lines.text: 1. Write content/week-03.json in the same shape as week-02.json.
2. In content/course.json set week 3's id to "week-03".
3. Push; the API checks the file at start-up and the week opens.

entries.title: Colours and type matched to revrag.ai
how: Colours were read from revrag.ai's live styles: violet accent, ink text, Inter.
Everything uses CSS variables, so a colour changes in one place.

lines.text: :root { --accent: #6645eb; }
Buttons, links, progress bars and diagrams all read this one variable.

entries.title: Sign in with Google
how: Server-side OAuth, as in sunny-side: the API sends you to Google, Google sends you back with a code, and the API swaps it for your verified email.
A signed state value plus a cookie stops someone else's sign-in from being slipped into yours.
The login token comes back after # in the link, which browsers never send to servers, so it stays out of logs.

lines.text: GET /api/fde/auth/google/start
302 → accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth?client_id=…&state=…
GET /api/fde/auth/google/callback?code=…&state=…
302 → https://fde-learning-rho.vercel.app/auth/callback#token=…

entries.title: God mode: this dashboard
how: Two checks on every request: your email is in ADMIN_EMAILS, and you signed in with Google (the token records how).
Everyone else gets a plain 404, so the page doesn't advertise that it exists.
The reactor, schematic and log are SVG and CSS animations drawn from live database counts.

lines.text: curl $API/api/fde/admin/overview -H 'Authorization: Bearer <a learner's token>'
404 {"detail":"Not Found"}
Your Google token gets the full overview.

entries.title: Redesign in the style of Revrag's voice and in-app agents, with a light/dark toggle
how: Agent-style hero, call pill and waveform, like the in-app agent you'll embed in P4.
Light is the default; the toggle sets data-theme on the page and is remembered per browser, applied before first paint so it never flashes.

lines.text: document.documentElement.dataset.theme = "dark"
Every colour is a CSS variable redefined under [data-theme="dark"], so one attribute flips the whole site.

entries.title: Only allowed email domains can use the site
how: ALLOWED_EMAIL_DOMAINS (for example revrag.ai) is checked at Google sign-in, password log-in and on every signed-in request.
Password sign-up closes once it's set, because only Google proves you own the address.
Addresses in ADMIN_EMAILS always get in, so the admin can't lock themselves out.

lines.text: Continue with Google → picks someone@gmail.com
Back on /login: "This site is only for … accounts."

entries.title: Build log on the assignment bus
how: Every shipped feature is one entry in content/build-log.json: where it lives, how it works and a tiny demo.
Each assignment card lists the features that practise it; the full timeline sits under the bus.
Every thread adds its entry in the same PR as the feature, so it stays current.

lines.text: content/build-log.json → append {"id": "my-feature", "date": "2026-11-13", …}
The API validates the file at start-up; a bad entry fails the tests, not the live site.

entries.title: Cohort view: every learner's progress, scores and who is stuck
how: GET /admin/learners reads every learner's items, project steps, submissions and quiz attempts in four queries and groups them in Python, behind the same require_admin gate as God mode.
A learner is flagged stuck when idle 3+ days, signed up 2+ days ago with nothing done, failed a week's graded quiz twice, or averages under 50% on practice.
Click a row for a drawer with every item, project links and quiz attempts (GET /admin/learners/{id}). Emails are never sent.
Other features add columns through LEARNER_EXTRAS[key] = fn(db, user_ids), which is how voice scorecards and project grades plug in.

lines.text: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $GOOGLE_ADMIN_TOKEN" $API/api/fde/admin/learners
{"summary": {"learners": 5, "stuck": 2, ...}, "learners": [{"name": "Rohan", "state": "stuck", "flags": [{"label": "Failed the week 1 quiz 2 times"}]}]}
In God mode the Cohort panel shows the same data, stuck learners first.

entries.title: Ask the coach: chat and voice agent that answers from the course
how: Every lesson, reading, project and voice prompt is cut into passages tagged with its course page; the graded quiz is left out so the coach can't leak answers.

A small BM25 keyword ranker picks the top 5 passages, boosted for the week you're on. With ANTHROPIC_API_KEY set, Claude answers from those passages only and cites them as [1], [2]; without it the coach quotes the passages.

The floating 'Ask the coach' pill opens a Revrag-style chat panel with source chips that link to the lesson. The mic button starts a LiveKit call: the voice-quiz worker runs in 'coach' mode and looks things up through /coach/internal/search.
Each question is saved (fde_coach_questions) for a 40-per-hour limit and shows up in God mode's terminal and the Coach AI chip.

demo.title: Ask a question from the command line

lines.text: curl -X POST https://fde-learnings.onrender.com/api/fde/coach/ask -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"question":"What does the waiter stand for?","week_id":"week-01"}'
{"answer":"The waiter is the API: it carries your request to the kitchen... [1]","mode":"ai","sources":[{"week_id":"week-01","item_id":"lesson-restaurant",...}]}
mode is "search" until ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is set on Render. Voice needs the LiveKit keys and the worker running.

entries.title: Assignment statuses update when work ships
how: A build-log entry can carry status_updates: which assignment moved, to what, why and when.
God mode shows whichever is newest, your own click or the latest update from shipped work, and says where it came from.
P1 and P2 still follow your course checklist until either of those sets them.

demo.title: Moving P3 forward from a PR

lines.text: "status_updates": [{"assignment": "w3-p3", "status": "doing", "note": "…", "at": "2026-11-12T16:40:00Z"}]
P3 card → IN PROGRESS · from the build log
Click a status yourself and your click wins until something newer ships.

status_updates.note: The signed-callback pattern is built and tested on this site (voice worker → API with a shared key; a wrong key gets 401). Still to do: your own P3 webhook from P2 to P1, plus the recording.
The site's agent-style UI (call pill, waveform) mirrors the in-app agent. Still to do: the dummy app with the real RevRag SDK and a staging key.
Rejecting requests without the right key header is built here (X-Worker-Key, constant-time compare). Still to do: the Lambda, DynamoDB and CloudWatch parts.
Google-only admin access, an email-domain allowlist and keys kept in env vars are all live on this site. Still to do: answer the 5 questionnaire questions.

entries.title: Auto-grading of P1 and P2 submissions
how: Saving a GitHub repo link on P1 or P2 starts a GitHub Actions run that clones the repo and installs, compiles, tests and builds it inside Docker, then calls the live links.
Learner code never runs in the API or next to a secret: a second job posts result.json back with a shared key.
Claude scores the rubric in content/grading.json from the repo, the checks and the learner's notes: 60 points of checks plus 40 of review, pass mark 70.
Learners see the score and feedback under their submission; God mode's Project grader lists every learner with a live pipeline, details and Regrade.

demo.title: Grade a P1 repo by hand

lines.text: python grader/run_checks.py --project P1 --repo https://github.com/<learner>/call-log --links '{"api_url": "https://..."}'
P1: 11/12 checks passed in 142s
Switch on: GRADER_GITHUB_TOKEN + GRADER_CALLBACK_KEY on Render, the same key as an Actions secret (docs/project-grading.md).

entries.title: Voice quiz scorecards and leaderboard
how: The voice coach's record_score tool now returns one result per question: correct or not, a note and the listed points the learner missed.

The worker keeps the call transcript from LiveKit's conversation events and posts it with the results; a second post when the room closes adds the goodbye lines, or saves an unscored card if they hung up early.
The API stores each call in the Neon table fde_voice_scorecards and works out the score and weak topics from the week's content, so the coach can't invent topics.

After the call the page waits for the card, then shows the score, topics to review (linked to their lessons), each answer and the transcript, plus a week or whole-course leaderboard of everyone's best call.

demo.title: Post a scorecard as the worker would

lines.text: curl -X POST $API/api/fde/internal/voice-quiz/calls -H "x-worker-key: $VOICE_WORKER_KEY" -d '{"call_id": "job-1", "user_id": 1, "week_id": "week-01", "complete": true, "questions": [{"id": "v1", "correct": true}, {"id": "v2", "correct": false, "missed": ["200 OK with JSON"]}], "transcript": [{"role": "coach", "text": "Hi!"}]}'
{"id": 1, "complete": true, "score": 1, "total": 2}
curl $API/api/fde/voice-quiz/leaderboard?week_id=week-01 -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
No new env vars: it uses the existing VOICE_WORKER_KEY and API_URL on the voice worker.

entries.title: Voice worker ready for free hosting on LiveKit Cloud
how: The voice_agent/ folder now builds on its own, which is what LiveKit Cloud's agent hosting needs.
The worker reads each week's questions from the API (API_URL) instead of a copy of content/ baked into the image.
LiveKit Cloud supplies the LiveKit keys; the worker only needs API_URL and VOICE_WORKER_KEY as secrets.

demo.title: Deploy it once from your laptop

lines.text: cd voice_agent && lk cloud auth && lk agent create --secrets-file .env.cloud
lk agent logs
Look for the worker registering as fde-voice-quiz, then try the mic in Ask the coach.

entries.title: Cohort view shows voice scorecards and project grades
how: cohort.py registers voice.voice_summary as LEARNER_EXTRAS["voice"]; grading.py already registers "grades".
Each row shows the latest voice score and top weak topics; the learner drawer lists their voice calls with weak topics and the full transcript.

lines.text: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $GOOGLE_ADMIN_TOKEN" $API/api/fde/admin/learners
{"name": "Priya", "voice": {"latest": {"score": 4, "total": 5}, "weak_topics": ["Status codes"], "calls": 2}, "grades": {"P1": {"score": 82, "status": "passed"}}}

entries.title: Cohort redesign: one row per learner, click for stats
how: The wide table (a column per week's quiz, voice, flags) became a list with one row per learner: avatar, name and status, the top flag or next item, a progress bar, score pills (quiz average, latest voice, project grades) and last active.
Each row is a button; clicking it opens a side drawer with stat tiles (progress, graded quizzes, voice, projects), the flags, weak topics, then every week, project link, voice call and quiz attempt.
Rows are a CSS grid, so on a phone they stack into cards instead of scrolling sideways. Colours come from the --gm-* tokens, so light and dark both work. No API changes.

demo.title: What a row is built from

lines.text: GET /api/fde/admin/learners  ->  one entry per learner
PN  Priya Nair  ON TRACK   29% ███░░░░   Quiz 90%  Voice 4/5  P1 92   1m ago  ›
RM  Rohan Mehta STUCK  ▲ Failed the week 1 quiz 2 times   17%   Quiz 0%   just now  ›
Click a row -> GET /admin/learners/{id} + /admin/voice-scorecards?user_id={id} fill the drawer.

entries.title: Assignment bus: one row per assignment, click for details
how: The bus used to be a grid of tall cards in columns. Now each week is a short list with one row per assignment: status light, title, kind and due date, progress (or how many deliverables), a 'built' count and the status pill.

Clicking a row opens the full card in the same side drawer the cohort view uses: deliverables, done-when, status buttons, what shipped work updated it, the features built on this site with their demos, and your note.
The drawer reads the assignment fresh from each refresh, so status clicks and notes update in place. On a phone rows wrap to two lines instead of squeezing into columns.

lines.text: WEEK 3                                                         0/3 done
● P3: a signed post-call webhook   2 deliverables  1 built  IN PROGRESS ›
○ Campaign call lifecycle diagram   1 deliverable            NOT STARTED ›
Click a row: the drawer shows the whole card, and Escape or a click outside closes it.

entries.title: Teacher mode: materials, Claude-written quizzes, project reviews
where: backend/app/models_teacher.py (fde_teachers, fde_materials, fde_material_files, fde_teacher_quizzes, fde_teacher_quiz_attempts, fde_grade_reviews, fde_announcements)
backend/app/grading.py (teacher_review on the learner's grade; overrides feed the cohort grades)
how: Teachers are emails in TEACHER_EMAILS or added from God mode's Teachers panel (the admin always counts). Like God mode, they must sign in with Google; everyone else gets a 404.

Materials: slides, PDFs, text and short videos upload into the database (MATERIAL_MAX_MB, default 25); long videos go in as YouTube/Loom/Vimeo/Drive links and play embedded. PDF and PPTX text (slides and speaker notes) is extracted for quizzes; for videos the teacher pastes a transcript or notes. Files are served through signed links that expire after 6 hours and support Range, so videos can seek.

Quizzes: the teacher picks materials (and/or the week's lessons), a count, difficulty and focus. Claude (QUIZ_MODEL, default claude-opus-5-5, structured JSON output) writes the questions in the background; bad ones are dropped. The teacher edits every question and publishes. Learners see answers only after submitting; the teacher sees per-learner results and how often each question was answered right.

Submissions: every saved GitHub link with the auto-grader's latest run. The teacher can check the repo on GitHub (public? README? last commit), regrade, and approve the score, set their own, or ask for changes with feedback. The learner sees the review on their grade card, and an override replaces the score in the cohort view.
Also: the cohort view (same as God mode, behind the teacher check), what learners ask the coach, and announcements that show on every learner's home page.

demo.title: From slides to a published quiz

lines.text: POST /api/fde/teacher/materials  (week-01, m1, kickoff.pptx, published=true)
201 {"kind": "slides", "text_chars": 4120, "has_text": true, "file_url": "/materials/7/file?exp=…&sig=…"}
POST /api/fde/teacher/quizzes/generate {"week_id": "week-01", "material_ids": [7], "count": 8}
202 {"status": "generating"} … then {"status": "draft", "count": 8, "message": "Claude wrote 8 questions. Check each one before you publish."}
POST /api/fde/teacher/quizzes/3/publish {"published": true}
Learners now see it under "From your teachers" on the week page. Reviewing P1: PUT /teacher/submissions/runs/12/review {"decision": "override", "score": 82, "feedback": "…"}.

entries.title: Voice worker redeploys itself from GitHub
how: A GitHub Action runs whenever voice_agent/ changes on main: it runs the worker's tests, installs the LiveKit CLI and runs lk agent deploy.
The LiveKit keys come from repository secrets; the worker's own secrets stay on LiveKit Cloud.
It can also be run by hand from the Actions tab (Run workflow).

lines.text: Merge a PR that touches voice_agent/ ...
Actions → Deploy voice worker → ✓ Test the worker → ✓ Deploy to LiveKit Cloud
No terminal needed; lk agent status in the log shows the new version Running.

entries.title: Voice coach: course answers, live transcript with references, Indian languages
how: Each English question is looked up in the course index before the voice LLM answers (for other languages the LLM calls search_course in English); the index now also holds teachers' published materials.
The worker sends the transcript, the references and "take me there" navigation to the browser over a LiveKit text stream (topic fde.coach).

The call panel shows the transcript with source chips, the mute button really mutes the mic, and the panel shrinks to a pill 10 seconds into a call, reopening when references arrive or the pill is clicked.
Learners pick a language before the call: English, Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam, Marathi, Bengali or Gujarati (Cartesia Sonic 3 voice, auto speech-to-text).

lines.text: Learner (Hindi): webhook kya hota hai?
refs → [1] Week 1 · Webhooks 101  ·  coach answers in Hindi
Learner: open the first one → navigate /weeks/week-01/…

entries.title: Coach: chat-or-voice chooser, screen actions, Sarvam voices
how: Ask the coach opens on a choice: Chat or Talk; Talk shows language chips.
The voice coach reads the page, scrolls and opens links/lessons through LiveKit RPC methods the browser registers; quiz answers and submits are refused in the browser.
Indian languages use Sarvam (LiveKit's recommendation) when SARVAM_API_KEY is set on the worker, else LiveKit Inference + Cartesia.

lines.text: Learner: scroll down and open week 2
screen.scroll {direction: down} → screen.click {label: "Week 2"} → note: Opened "Week 2"
Learner: answer question 1 for me → Left "…" for you to press

entries.title: Design system pass: calmer, crafted UI across every page
how: One token set in styles.css: 9-step type scale, 4px spacing scale, 6/8/12 radii, neutral surfaces; violet only for interactive, selected or in-progress.
Removed gradients, glows, gradient text, pill-shaped everything and looping decoration; tabs are underlined, records are bordered lists with dividers.
Home leads with your progress and next week instead of a phone mock; login is a focused form; top bar uses icon nav links and a one-button theme switch.
God mode keeps its data views but sits on the site's surfaces (no grid, scanline, glow or spinning).

lines.text: .tc-tabs button[aria-selected="true"] { color: var(--text); border-bottom-color: var(--accent); }
Teacher tabs, course tabs and God mode filters now share one look
Before/after screenshots: project files ui-polish/
